## Analysis

The dense-core/fringe run produced \(n=31\), \(114\) sums, and \(105\) differences, yet scored below the unstructured incumbent. Combined with the failed exhaustive endpoint-fringe sweep, this now refutes dense intervals with independently optimized fringes as the main route forward: extra core elements create too many sums and differences proportionally. The persistent \(n=17\) ceiling instead suggests searching near sets whose sum and difference collision structures are initially balanced, then introducing controlled asymmetry. A nearly symmetric construction provides that neutral baseline while sharply restricting the search geometry.
